findings.address_as_written: Resolution No. 34244 (New Series) - Larsen Park dedication
findings.description: The Board of Park Commissioners received the Supervisors' resolution asking the Mayor to set a day to dedicate the land the late Carl G. Larsen had deeded to the city for a park, in the blocks between Ulloa and Wawona Streets and Nineteenth and Twentieth Avenues.

findings.address_as_written: Coit Bequest advisory committee - combination of monument and memorial
findings.description: The advisory committee on Lillie Hitchcock Coit's bequest agreed that the memorial to the city's original volunteer fire department, for which her executors had chosen the sculptor Haig Patigian, would stand in Pioneer Park on Telegraph Hill, and that the roughly $185,000 her will gave for beautifying the city would go to architectural and landscape treatment of the park, $85,000 of it for landscaping; it appointed Arthur Brown, Jr. architect and John McLaren landscape engineer.

findings.address_as_written: Coit Memorial - discussion of plans and estimates
findings.description: Shown preliminary plans and estimates for the Coit Memorial, the Coit bequest advisory committee told Arthur Brown, Jr. to prepare detailed plans and specifications for a tower only by November 24, 1931, and asked Supervisor James B. McSheehy to seek a rezoning of the land around Telegraph Hill so future skyscrapers would not block the view from the memorial or spoil it.

findings.description: Lewis F. Byington urged the Coit bequest advisory committee to build the memorial tower at least 250 feet high and offered to raise money for it; the architects held the planned height architecturally right but said the column could later be lengthened in units of about 26 feet, up to 250 feet, if its foundations and the steel in its fluted section were strengthened now.

findings.description: After fifteen bids for the Coit memorial tower were opened, the lowest about $77,400, and with the advisory committee wanting a contract signed before the new Art Commission was created, the Board of Park Commissioners authorized its president to award the contract to the lowest responsible bidder and set aside up to $1,500 of the memorial fund to strengthen the foundations and the fluted column for a possible future increase in height.
